prompt: Marginal utility measures

options.label: A
options.text: The satisfaction from all units combined

options.label: B
options.text: Income remaining after a purchase

options.label: C
options.text: The extra utility from one more unit

options.label: D
options.text: The average price of a good

options.label: E
options.text: The cost of all consumption

explanation: Marginal utility is the change in total utility from an additional unit consumed.

prompt: Total utility measures

options.label: A
options.text: Income divided by total spending

options.label: B
options.text: The number of available substitutes

options.label: C
options.text: Only the satisfaction from the next unit

options.label: D
options.text: The satisfaction from all units consumed

options.label: E
options.text: The price of the last unit

explanation: Total utility adds the satisfaction generated by the consumed units.

prompt: Diminishing marginal utility means that, as consumption rises,

options.label: A
options.text: Each successive unit provides more satisfaction

options.label: B
options.text: Total utility must fall after the first unit

options.label: C
options.text: All units provide zero satisfaction

options.label: D
options.text: The price must rise after each unit

options.label: E
options.text: Successive units provide smaller utility gains

explanation: Diminishing marginal utility concerns smaller additions to total utility as consumption increases.

prompt: If the next unit has positive marginal utility, consuming it will

options.label: A
options.text: Reduce total utility

options.label: B
options.text: Necessarily double total utility

options.label: C
options.text: Leave total utility unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: Increase total utility

options.label: E
options.text: Make total utility equal price

explanation: Positive marginal utility adds satisfaction to the previous total.

prompt: If a unit has zero marginal utility, consuming it will

options.label: A
options.text: Reduce all previous utility

options.label: B
options.text: Make total utility zero

options.label: C
options.text: Necessarily increase the good's price

options.label: D
options.text: Leave total utility unchanged

options.label: E
options.text: Increase total utility by one

explanation: Zero marginal utility means the extra unit adds no satisfaction to the total.

prompt: If the next unit has negative marginal utility, consuming it will

options.label: A
options.text: Leave total utility unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: Increase marginal utility on every unit

options.label: C
options.text: Eliminate the budget constraint

options.label: D
options.text: Increase total utility

options.label: E
options.text: Reduce total utility

explanation: Negative marginal utility means the extra unit subtracts from total satisfaction.

prompt: A rational consumer compares the last dollar spent on different goods by using

options.label: A
options.text: Marginal utility divided by price

options.label: B
options.text: Price divided by total utility

options.label: C
options.text: Total utility divided by income

options.label: D
options.text: Total spending divided by quantity

options.label: E
options.text: Marginal utility multiplied by price

explanation: MU/P measures the additional satisfaction obtained per dollar spent on a good.

prompt: A consumer's budget constraint reflects

options.label: A
options.text: Limited income and available goods’ prices

options.label: B
options.text: An unlimited ability to borrow

options.label: C
options.text: The requirement to buy equal quantities

options.label: D
options.text: Only the total utility of the first purchase

options.label: E
options.text: Only the consumer's favorite good

explanation: Income limits affordable purchases, and prices determine how much each bundle costs.

prompt: In the rational consumer-choice model, consumers seek to

options.label: A
options.text: Buy equal quantities regardless of preferences

options.label: B
options.text: Minimize satisfaction from purchases

options.label: C
options.text: Maximize the price paid per unit

options.label: D
options.text: Maximize total utility subject to constraints

options.label: E
options.text: Maximize spending regardless of utility

explanation: Consumers choose the affordable combination giving the greatest total satisfaction.

prompt: Marginal cost of an activity is

options.label: A
options.text: Total benefit divided by quantity

options.label: B
options.text: The cost already paid for all past units

options.label: C
options.text: The activity's total cost at zero output

options.label: D
options.text: The fixed benefit from past choices

options.label: E
options.text: The cost of one additional unit

explanation: Marginal cost measures the extra expense or sacrifice caused by an additional unit of activity.

prompt: Marginal benefit of an activity is

options.label: A
options.text: The fixed cost of starting the activity

options.label: B
options.text: Income remaining after the activity

options.label: C
options.text: The benefit of all previous units combined

options.label: D
options.text: Total cost divided by the number of units

options.label: E
options.text: The additional benefit from one more unit

explanation: Marginal benefit measures the extra gain from increasing the activity.

prompt: If the next unit's marginal benefit exceeds its marginal cost, a person should

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the activity

options.label: B
options.text: Ignore the additional benefit

options.label: C
options.text: Reduce the activity to zero

options.label: D
options.text: Maintain the quantity in every case

options.label: E
options.text: Choose based only on past spending

explanation: The extra unit adds more benefit than cost, increasing net benefit.

prompt: If the last unit's marginal cost exceeds its marginal benefit, removing that unit will

options.label: A
options.text: Reduce net benefit

options.label: B
options.text: Make every cost a sunk cost

options.label: C
options.text: Leave net benefit unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: Necessarily remove all total benefit

options.label: E
options.text: Increase net benefit

explanation: Removing the unit saves more cost than the benefit sacrificed, increasing net benefit.

prompt: On a standard graph with falling MB and rising MC, the optimal activity level is where

options.label: A
options.text: Total benefit equals zero

options.label: B
options.text: MC equals zero

options.label: C
options.text: MB equals MC

options.label: D
options.text: Average benefit equals fixed cost

options.label: E
options.text: Total cost is highest

explanation: Net benefit rises before MB meets MC and falls beyond it. Their intersection identifies the optimum.

prompt: A sunk cost is

options.label: A
options.text: A benefit from additional consumption

options.label: B
options.text: The cost of the next unit

options.label: C
options.text: A cost that varies only with future choices

options.label: D
options.text: A refundable deposit

options.label: E
options.text: A cost already incurred that cannot be recovered

explanation: A sunk cost cannot be changed by the current decision, so it should not determine the marginal choice.

prompt: A student has paid a nonrefundable concert fee but now dislikes the show. The decision to stay should depend on

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the student can recover the fee by staying

options.label: B
options.text: Future benefits versus future opportunity costs

options.label: C
options.text: The fee already paid alone

options.label: D
options.text: The total fees paid by everyone attending

options.label: E
options.text: The fee divided by the number of songs

explanation: The fee is unrecoverable either way. Staying should be evaluated using its remaining benefits and costs.

prompt: A benefit received from a past decision that cannot be changed now should

options.label: A
options.text: Require the activity to continue forever

options.label: B
options.text: Replace the need to compare MB and MC

options.label: C
options.text: Determine the next unit's cost

options.label: D
options.text: Be excluded from the current marginal comparison

options.label: E
options.text: Be counted again for every future unit

explanation: A fixed past benefit is the same under the current alternatives. It does not change the net gain from the next unit.

options.label: B
options.text: The total number of dollars spent

options.label: D

options.label: E
options.text: The total utility from all goods

explanation: Dividing marginal utility by price expresses the satisfaction gained from the last dollar allocated to the good.

prompt: If MUx/Px exceeds MUy/Py, an affordable reallocation toward X and away from Y can

options.text: Require equal quantities of X and Y

options.label: D
options.text: Make the budget irrelevant

options.text: Prove that X has a lower price

options.label: D
